🔥 MixForge — Help & Guide

MixForge is a batch concept-art tool that runs on your own machine over ComfyUI (SDXL Juggernaut + House LoRAs). You blend reference art and prompts into rough concepts, breed the good ones, polish and upscale a favourite, then spin it into a full turnaround character sheet — all without leaving the browser.

Welcome▲ top

What MixForge is

Every render is a weighted mix of reference images (which carry style & palette) and your prompt (which carries the idea). MixForge organises that into a five-step assembly line: explore wide, breed the winners, then finish one hero image. Nothing is destructive — every image you make is saved to a stage folder and stays in your Gallery forever.

Local & private. MixForge talks to a ComfyUI instance on cuda:0 — you can see it live in the top bar. No images leave your computer.

The 6-stage pipeline

1 · Discover› 2 · Evolve› 3 · Refine› 4 · Upres› 5 · Character Sheet› 6 · Final
  • Discover — batch exploration. Throw references + a prompt at the wall and generate many rough candidates.
  • Evolve — pick two favourites and breed them into a batch of children; grow a tree of variations.
  • Refine — lock one image and polish it (fix anatomy, add a detail) without losing the design.
  • Upres — tiled-diffusion upscale to 2× / 4× with smart, on-theme detail.
  • Character Sheet — turn the finished hero into a multi-view turnaround with a head close-up.
  • Final — a high-detail upscale of the whole sheet into the FINAL folder: the shareable end product.

Full Run — every render also has a red Full Run » button. One click walks that image through Refine → Upres → Character Sheet → Final automatically as a single job, and the app switches screens as it goes so you can watch it move down the line.

You do not have to use every stage. A quick idea might stop at Discover; a hero asset walks the whole line.

Core vs Project prompt

The prompt bar has two tabs:

  • Project — what you're designing right now ("a modern post-apocalyptic survivor"). Change this constantly.
  • Core — your house style: the long, mostly-fixed block (medium, lighting, quality words, standing art rules) that rides on every render so your whole set looks like one artist made it.
Keep the Project prompt SHORT. Concrete nouns in the prompt beat everything else — a clause like "man in dragon armor holding a harpoon, purple eyes and spear energy" stamps dragon armor, a polearm and a purple wash onto every render, no matter what your references say (that one line once made an entire 50-founder Night Run identical). Describe only the concept; let references, wildcards and MISC define the costume. Always-on signatures like purple eyes belong in Pinned anchors (see Discover), where they're masked to their body region and can't tint the rest of the design.
Style words are a nudge, not a lock. A phrase like "in the style of <artist>" biases the model but will not reliably suppress unwanted content (e.g. modern clothing) on its own. If something keeps sneaking in, the reliable levers are: put the opposite in the negative prompt, lower the offending reference's weight, or add an explicit positive ("heavy plate armor, leather"). See Recipes.

Interface tour▲ top

The window, labeled

Everything lives on one screen. The stepper across the top is your only navigation — click any stage to switch to it.

Carrying a render forward

The pipeline is glued together by one gesture. Every render has a Use this → button (top-right of the big preview, and on gallery thumbs). Its colour tells you where it goes:

Use in Refine → Use in Upres → Use in Character Sheet →

Clicking it drops that image into the next stage's input slot and switches you there. You can also drag any thumbnail onto a stage's "drop a render here" panel. Stages are freely reachable from the stepper at any time.

Queue from anywhere, any time. While something is rendering, GO becomes + Queue — every stage can stack more work onto the backlog, from any screen, and jobs run in turn. The Monitor shows the backlog (with per-job ✕ to cancel) and a prominent Est. done clock projected from your real per-stage averages. Error banners now carry a dismiss ✕, and the whole rendering state survives a browser refresh.

Stage 1Discover explore▲ top

The wide-net stage. Load a few reference images, write what you're designing, set a batch size, and generate a spread of rough candidates. This is where a look is found.

Subjects & weights

Each Subject bucket (A, B, C…) holds one or more reference images that share a role. MixForge feeds them through IPAdapter, so they contribute style, palette and silhouette — not literal copying. The Weight slider sets how loud that bucket is in the mix; Range ± jitters the weight a little per render so a batch explores around your setting instead of repeating.

Rule of thumb. References drive the look; the prompt drives the idea. If a reference's outfit is bleeding through too strongly, lower its Weight rather than fighting it in text.

Weights auto-normalize. Under the hood, every render's rolled Subject weights are scaled so they total exactly 1.0 — your sliders set ratios, not absolute strength. This keeps references firmly in charge: totals below ~1 used to hand the design to the checkpoint's own taste (everything drifted fantasy no matter what your refs said). A bucket whose roll lands on 0 still sits that render out — that's Range doing its job — and the buckets that did participate split the full 1.0 between them. A solo bucket rides at 1.0.

The bucket is now the quality gate. Because each render draws one image from each bucket and follows it strongly, every weak image in a folder is a guaranteed weak render — a product photo gives you product-shot proportions, a monochrome sheet gives you a monochrome character, a female-form ref gives you a female form. Curate hard: every image in an enabled bucket should be one you'd be happy to see steer a render on its own.

Novelty & Strength

Novelty adds unexpected on-theme elements that aren't in any reference — the same amount every render, but different surprises each time, so results stay on-model while still varying. Every rolled term now lands as a masked conditioning branch aimed at its body region: a helmet term conditions only the head zone, boots only the feet, and terms from the shared pool cover the whole figure. Nothing rides quietly in the prompt tail anymore — if a term rolled, it's being painted. The ⓘ recipe shows each term with a chip naming where it went (→ head, → torso, → figure…). Edit wildcard list… opens the word libraries the surprises are drawn from.

Pinned anchors — always-on signatures

Some design elements aren't surprises — they're by design, on every render. Pinned anchors live in prompts/novelty/pinned.txt, one per line as region: term:

head: glowing purple eyes
torso: a scorched clan sigil on the chest

Each line becomes a masked branch on every Discover, Refine and Evolve render — always present, but physically unable to leak outside its region. Valid regions: head, torso, shoulders, hands, feet, figure (whole body). The file is read fresh each render, so edits apply immediately — no restart. Every render's ⓘ recipe lists its anchors with a PINNED → region chip.

Why not just put it in the prompt? A prompt is one signal covering the whole canvas — "glowing purple eyes" in the Project prompt tints armor, weapons and energy effects purple, because the model hears "purple" while painting everything. Masked to the head box, the color can't reach the torso. If a signature keeps bleeding, it belongs here, not in the prompt.

Injecting the unexpected — Novelty vs MISC, and the body-region map

Your Subject buckets define who the character is. Two systems add elements that are not in any Subject reference — one works with words, one works with images — and both are aimed at the same semantic body regions so a helmet lands on the head, boots land on the feet:

Novelty — injecting with WORDS

Draws surprise terms from the word libraries in prompts/novelty/<region>/ (headwear.txt, gloves.txt, footware.txt…) plus the shared pool global.txt — and conditions every term onto the canvas through its body-region mask (pool terms use a whole-figure mask, merged into one branch so they can't spawn a second character).

  • Novelty amount — how many surprises per render.
  • Masked landing — a rolled term is painted, not whispered; the ⓘ recipe's region chips are the receipt.
  • Cheap, endless variety; the model imagines the item, so styles blend naturally.

MISC — injecting with IMAGES

Pulls one random reference photo from each category folder in misc/ (helmets, boots, materials…) and applies it as an attention-masked IPAdapter branch only inside that body region. Materials apply as a light whole-figure surface style.

  • Per-category Chance — each category rolls its own participation per render (default 30%); on a hit, ONE random pick lands on its region. 30% ≈ a render wears 1–2 accessories, not the whole shop. The always-on 5-category stack was the old conformity engine.
  • Strength ~0.8 — below that, picks don't visibly land. The shared Strength bar sits at the top of the card.
  • Keep character images out of misc/random/ — accessories and textures only.
  • Anatomy safety: leg/feet/hand branches run at reduced weight and release at 50% of sampling — they skin the limb the skeleton drew, they never draw a limb of their own (the 3-leg fix).
Which to use? Novelty for open-ended surprise ("give me ideas"); MISC when you have a specific item or material you want on the character. They stack — every render logs its picks in the recipe (ⓘ), so a keeper is reproducible.

Style & Pose

The other two input tabs:

  • Style — an optional IPAdapter reference used purely for look (colour, rendering, mood) with no attempt to copy its subject.
  • Pose — drop a figure and MixForge extracts an OpenPose skeleton (ControlNet) so your character stands the way you want. Keep it to a single figure here; multi-figure turnarounds belong in the Character Sheet stage. The canvas auto-matches the pose's aspect so nothing stretches.

Aspect · Draft · Batch

  • Aspect — 9:16 portrait16:9 landscape Renders at SDXL's native ~1.2 MP for that shape.
  • Draft / Sketch — cut only the sampling steps (30 → 18 → 10) for fast, rougher passes so you can scan many ideas cheaply, then re-run the keepers at Full. Resolution stays baseline at every level: steps are what drive render time, and keeping full resolution means a draft reads true (no off-native over-saturation) and can be sent straight to Refine.
  • Batch — how many candidates this GO produces. Each gets its own seed (and jittered weights, if Range > 0).

Stage 2Evolve breed▲ top

Found two candidates you love? Evolve crossbreeds them. It fuses both parents' reference embeddings and generates a batch of children that share DNA from each — then you promote a favourite child to be a new parent and grow the tree.

Parents & progeny

Click Choose from Output under Parent A and Parent B and pick any two renders. Set Progeny per Batch and hit GO — the children appear as a row in the Evolve Tree on the right, hanging off their two parents. Use any child as a new parent to keep breeding down a promising line.

Weight · mutation · fidelity

  • Parent Weight — full-left = 100% Parent A, full-right = 100% Parent B, centre = an even 50/50 blend of the two.
  • Mutation — adds NEW wildcard elements that neither parent had, placed on the right body part (a helm on the head, boots on the feet). Higher % = more regions get an addition, and the parents grip a little looser to make room. Head-region mutations are automatically strength-capped so a hot roll never shatters the face.
  • Fidelity — when Parent Weight is lopsided (≥ 75/25), this dial sets how literally the dominant parent's signature features (a glowing head, a distinctive mask) are copied onto the children. ~40% is the sweet spot — a human wearing the signature; higher trades anatomy for carry-over.

Evolve children land in their own EVOLVE gallery tab, and the parent picker only offers raw stock — Discover renders and other Evolve children — never downstream Refine/Upres products.

Solo Dice 🎲 — variations of ONE parent

Each parent slot has a small ⏻ chip. Turn one parent OFF and the other's chip becomes a 🎲 dice — GO now rolls variations of that single parent: same core character (a wizard stays a wizard holding a staff), fresh takes. Per child, the roll jitters the identity grip and release point, picks a stance, and applies Mutation as the novelty control — Mutation 0 = pure re-rolls, no surprises. The Parent Weight card greys out in dice mode (there's nothing to balance). Solo batches show in the tree as [parent] × 🎲.

Stage 3Refine polish▲ top

You've chosen the one. Refine does an img2img pass over it at low denoise to clean up anatomy and add a requested detail — keeping the same character and pose. Refine always outputs baseline resolution: if you hand it a sub-baseline image, it's upscaled to the ~1.5 MP sweet spot (aspect preserved) before the pass, so a rough sketch comes back full-size and finished.

Polish vs change

The Strength slider (denoise) is the whole story here:

  • ~0.35 — polish. Sharpen detail, fix small anatomy, keep the design essentially identical.
  • ~0.5+ — fix anatomy / add elements. Anything typed in Change / add is applied with heavy weight so it definitely happens — but the image drifts more from the original.

Leave the Change box empty for a pure clean-up pass — polish mode holds the design hard: the exact outfit, headwear and colors are explicitly preserved, so a turban stays a turban.

Headroom law. Refine re-frames its input to Discover proportions before the pass — figure capped at ~84% of canvas height, feet anchored near the bottom, real headroom above (scale-down only, nothing is ever stretched). Heads never kiss the top edge again, whatever you feed it.

Novelty in Refine

Refine has the same Novelty knobs as Discover — the identical code path. At Novelty 0 nothing is injected and nothing changes that you didn't ask for; raise it and each render can roll wildcard elements on top of your Change instruction (which keeps priority). Use it to explore within a design you already like.

Rescue feet & hands

With Rescue feet & hands ON (the default), Refine runs an extra masked pass over the toes and fingers to fix the usual SDXL extremity mush. It cleans what's there — it won't remove an extra limb, so if a hand has six fingers, nudge Strength up instead.

Stage 4Upres upscale▲ top

The finishing enlarge, with a Mode toggle:

  • Magnific default — a SUPIR creative upscale that reconstructs materials and invents plausible micro-detail, Magnific-style. The design is locked at every creativity level — it invents texture, never a new character.
  • Enhanced — the tiled-diffusion upscale (UltimateSDUpscale + 4x-UltraSharp): smart on-theme detail (buckles, leather wrinkles, resolved shapes) while keeping the illustrated look.

Enhanced vs Magnific — when to use which

Magnific is the default and the usual right answer: at ~10% creativity it's a faithful enlargement (same design, genuinely reconstructed detail — engraving, weave, grain); at the default ~70% it invents rich material micro-detail while the silhouette, palette and design stay put. Each mode remembers its own creativity setting. In Magnific, 4× runs SUPIR to 2× and then the tiler doubles it gently so the invented detail is preserved, not re-imagined. Reach for Enhanced when you want the classic tile-diffusion look or Magnific reinterprets something you care about (exposed faces can get adventurous at high creativity).

Size & Creativity

  • Final size — 2× for a quick high-res, 4× for a print-scale hero. 4× is slower (more tiles).
  • Creativity (Enhanced) — low = a faithful sharpen; high = reinvents detail and resolves shapes (but can drift). ~35% is the sweet spot.
  • Creativity (Magnific) — drives SUPIR's structure grip and restoration. ~10% = faithful upres · ~70% (default) = rich invented detail · 90%+ = heavy invention, shape still held.
Steps drive time, not size. A 4× upscale isn't 4× the wait — tile count and step count are what cost you. Grab a coffee for a big one and watch progress in the top bar.

Stage 5Character Sheet turnaround▲ top

The payoff. Your finished hero becomes the sole reference, and a multi-figure pose map lays out back · left profile · front · right profile of the same character on a wide canvas — with a big on-model head close-up in its own column on the far right.

Turnaround pose maps

Pick a map from the Turnaround pose map dropdown; the preview shows the skeletons that will be drawn. The default, v4.jpg, is the battle-tested 4-view layout. Under the hood the sheet stage uses a much stronger pose enforcer than the other stages (the same one behind the original "perfect" 2024 model sheets), holds it for the whole render, and gives each view its own masked mini-prompt — that's what makes true back views and strict profiles land reliably. Because a character sheet needs one strong identity — not three references fighting — this stage uses only your single finished image as the reference.

Why the head is composited, not posed. Rendering a head from face keypoints proved unreliable (faceless helmets made the model invent a generic face; the stronger pose model drew the landmark dots literally). Instead the close-up is cropped from your reference (face-detect, with headroom for helmets and horns), enlarged to a fixed big box, its backdrop re-matched to the sheet's grey, and appended as a new column on the right — it can never cover a figure, and it always matches the hero exactly.

Ref weight & head

Ref weight (1.0 recommended) controls how tightly every view clamps to the hero's identity. Push it up if a view drifts off-model; ease it down slightly if the figures look stiff or cloned. The content reference is also held almost to the end of sampling here (vs. released early on posed single renders) precisely so the face and outfit survive across all the views.

Stage 6Final finish▲ top

The last mile. Final runs the same tiled-diffusion upscaler as Upres, but over the whole character sheet, and drops the result into the FINAL folder — the file you actually hand to a modeler or client. The wide sheet aspect is preserved exactly (a 2× of 1812×768 comes out 3624×1536).

  • Creativity defaults high (~70%) — sheet figures render small, so their faces and cloth need real re-invention, not just sharpening. Blurry faces come back crisp.
  • Detail put back, not made up — the Upres render the sheet was built from quietly rides along as a reference, anchoring the re-invented detail to the character's true costume. Stitches and buckles that blurred away at sheet size return on-design.
  • Same controls as Upres: 2× / 4× and the Creativity slider.

Full Run — one click to the end

Any render (a Discovery rough, a Refine, an Upres) has a red Full Run » button — the big one on the preview and lightbox, and the small » chip on gallery thumbnails. One click runs Refine → Upres → Character Sheet → Final as a single job:

  • The app switches stages as the job moves, exactly as if you clicked through yourself — you can watch the image walk the line.
  • The Monitor reads honestly: "2 of 4 — Upscaling".
  • Every intermediate lands in its own gallery tab (REFINE, UPSCALE, SHEET), and the finished piece lands in FINAL.
  • Abort stops the whole chain cleanly. Evolve is intentionally skipped.

🌙 Night Run — unattended batches▲ top

Night Run is MixForge running while you sleep: configure a large batch in one modal, press GO, and come back to a pipeline's worth of finished work. The 🌙 button (top-right tools, next to Monitor) opens it.

One modal, one GO

  • Source — Fresh Discovery Batch (N new renders using your current Subjects, Novelty, MISC — exactly like pressing GO yourself) or Existing Folder (a native picker; every image in the folder is snapshotted and processed).
  • Pipeline depth — the dot-and-line selector sets how far every render travels: Discovery only → Refine → Upres → Character Sheet → Final. Sheet/Final need a turnaround pose map picked first, and no stage is ever skipped in the middle.
  • Run summary — counts plus a projected Est. finish time computed from your real per-stage averages, before you commit.

Settings are snapshotted at GO — change sliders afterwards freely; the running Night Run keeps the recipe it launched with.

The Evolve pass

Toggle on auto-paired Evolve and a small founder pool breeds a much wider progeny pool (10 founders can drive 100 progeny). Pairing is automatic and diversity-seeking: for each group, parent A is drawn at random and parent B is the most different founder the picker can find — a completely different drawn source reference counts most, lowest wildcard overlap breaks ties. Never self-pairs; a single founder switches to Solo Dice. Every child rolls a fresh parent blend (anywhere from 12/88 to 88/12) and mutations run LARGE (65–100%, rolled per pairing — the manual Evolve slider is ignored overnight). Only the progeny continue downstream; founders stop after breeding.

Diversity in = diversity out. Blending two near-identical parents produces the same child at any blend ratio, and mutation can only decorate on top. If a whole run comes out samey, the usual culprit isn't Evolve — it's a homogeneous founder pool, most often caused by an over-specific Project prompt stamping every founder with the same costume.

Resume · abort · monitoring

  • Crash-safe. Every stage transition is journaled to night-runs/<run-id>/. If the app or PC restarts, the run resumes automatically — completed work is never re-rendered, shortfalls are topped up.
  • Abort. Re-open the 🌙 modal while a run is active: GO becomes a red ABORT Night Run. It stops future dispatch, interrupts only the run's own render, and keeps everything already produced. Manual jobs in the queue are untouched.
  • Monitor. The run appears in the Monitor as night_run jobs, the Est. done — whole Night Run strip projects the true finish time (founders + progeny + every remaining stage), and the main UI follows along stage-by-stage just like a Full Run.
  • One Night Run at a time; a failed branch never stops the others (the run ends completed with errors instead).
Overnight recipe. 10–20 founders · Evolve ON at 60–100 progeny · depth Refine + Upres. You wake to a wide, varied pool already polished and enlarged — cull in the gallery over coffee, then Full-Run the keepers.

Gallery & voting▲ top

The strip along the bottom is every render you've ever made, newest first. Click any thumb to load it into the big preview. The ▲ triangle expands the gallery into a full grid; the ▼ triangle hides it completely — the header row with the tabs and triangles always stays, so it's one click back.

Folder filters

Each render lands in the folder named for the furthest stage it reached, and the tabs filter by it:

YoursAllDISCOVEREVOLVEREFINEUPSCALESHEETFINALTESTS

Thumbnail borders are tinted with the same stage colours, so you can read a render's history at a glance.

Hovering a thumb reveals its action chips: → sends it to the next stage, the red » fires a Full Run, and ✕ deletes (to trash). Thumbs can also be dragged — onto a stage's input panel, or straight into Evolve's Parent A / B slots.

On the short, wide Character Sheet and Final screens the gallery automatically shows two rows of thumbs instead of leaving the reclaimed space blank.

Voting & info

👍 / 👎 under the preview (and on thumbs) tag renders you like or dislike — a quick way to mark keepers for later.

The ⓘ button reveals a render's recipe: prompt, seed, weights, checkpoint, and which stage produced it. Apply & clean tidies the current filter.

Options · Models & LoRAs▲ top

The ⚙ button (top-right tools) opens Options — a category sidebar with Main Model (checkpoint + Baseline CFG) and LoRAs. The panel remembers where you were — category, tab and scroll — across close/reopen.

Three KINDS of LoRA — folder = kind

LoRAs live in three folders (LoRA\style, LoRA\subject, LoRA\detail) shown as three tabs, because the three kinds do different jobs and apply at different stages:

  • Style — the house look (ink, anime, realism). Applies to every stage. Runs its vocabulary (CLIP) at 35% of the weight so a hot style can't drag designs toward its training subject.
  • Subject — design DNA (wires, biotech, fractals, robot parts, geometric couture). Applies in Discover and Evolve at full CLIP — the vocabulary IS the point — and Refine automatically re-applies the source render's subject set at half weight so the DNA survives polishing. Each row has a Chance slider: it auto-shares across enabled subject LoRAs (one at 100% always fires; two at 100% fire ~50% each) so stacked LoRAs deal different DNA to different renders instead of all fighting on every one.
  • Detail — micro-texture enhancers. Apply only in Upres · Sheet · Final, UNet-only (CLIP 0), so they enrich finished pixels without re-interpreting the prompt.

Every render's ⓘ recipe has a LoRAs fired list showing exactly which LoRAs (with kind, weight and CLIP) touched that image — the reproducibility receipt now that LoRA sets vary per stage and per render. Each row also has a CLIP: auto button to pin a custom CLIP strength when a specific LoRA needs to deviate from its kind's doctrine.

Pure prompt mode. A Discover batch with no Subject buckets is allowed — the render is driven by prompt + LoRAs alone. That's the exploration lane for harvesting a subject LoRA's native look (big silhouette-breaking shapes that references would otherwise tame) — keep the best and drop them into a bucket as new reference DNA.

Base Model — the checkpoint every stage renders with (same setting as the top-bar Model select). Drop any full checkpoint .safetensors into MixForge\comfyUI\, hit Refresh, and it appears in the picker marked (yours). The scanner reads each file's actual tensor header, so a LoRA mis-filed as a checkpoint gets an amber "not a base model" warning instead of a mid-render failure.

Drop .safetensors files into the folder shown and hit Refresh. Trigger words and a preview thumbnail are pulled from Civitai automatically (the first scan hashes each file, so it can take a moment) — each LoRA row shows its full-height preview tile on the left, always vivid even when the LoRA is off. These LoRAs are what make an entire MixForge set feel like one artist's hand.

Everything auto-saves. Every toggle, weight and CFG change in this panel persists on its own a half-second after you touch it — no Save click needed, and a browser refresh always comes back exactly as you left it. A locked or mid-copy file in the folder is skipped harmlessly, so you can drop files in while renders are running.

Style without the content drag. A LoRA pushes through two channels: the UNet half carries the rendering (ink density, linework, shading) and the CLIP half carries the vocabulary — the concept associations that quietly pull every design toward the LoRA's training subject ("graphic novel character" → fantasy hero). MixForge now runs House LoRAs with UNet at your full slider weight but CLIP at 35% of it, so you can run a style LoRA hot (≈0.9–1.0) for a rock-steady house look without it normalizing your designs. If every render still drifts toward one archetype at a high weight, the LoRA's vocabulary is winning anyway — lower its weight before blaming your references.

Recipes & tips▲ top

Explore fast, then commit

Turn Draft ON, set Batch to 6–8, and fire several GOs to scan a look cheaply. Then Draft OFF and re-run only the keepers at full quality before carrying one into Refine.

Something keeps sneaking in

Modern clothing, gears, a colour you didn't ask for? Don't rely on style words. Add the opposite to the negative prompt, drop the guilty reference's weight, and add an explicit positive ("heavy plate armor"). Fix it at the source.

Keep identity through the sheet

Only send a finished hero (post-Refine, ideally post-Upres) into Character Sheet. A rough Discover render doesn't have enough locked detail for the views to agree. Nudge Ref weight up if a view drifts.

Weights, not wording, for references

When two Subjects fight, the Weight sliders resolve it faster than any amount of prompt surgery. Use Range ± to let a batch explore around a weight you're unsure of.

Buttons & shortcuts▲ top

GO — run the current stage · Use this → — carry a render to the next stage · Drag a thumb onto an input slot to load it · 👍 / 👎 — vote · ⓘ — recipe · ⚙ — House LoRAs config · Expand ▲ — full gallery grid · ? — this guide.

Tip: you can deep-link a stage with ?stage=refine (or discover / evolve / upres / sheet) on the URL, and open config with ?open=config.

MixForge runs locally over ComfyUI · SDXL Juggernaut XI + House LoRAs · IPAdapter + OpenPose ControlNet. Every image stays on your machine.
